title: System health
intro: The page to open when something is wrong. Every row says what breaks for a caller if that part stops, not just whether it is green.
verdict_ok_body: Everything a call needs is running. One thing is broken that a caller never sees: notification emails cannot leave your network.
verdict_degraded_title: Callers are waiting too long for an answer
verdict_degraded_body: The language model is taking about four seconds to start replying. Calls still complete, but people talk over the agent because they assume it did not hear them.
verdict_down_body: SIP registration was refused 6 minutes ago, so every caller hears the line ring out. The agent itself is fine — this is between Tel-Agent and your provider, and a wrong password is the usual cause.
service_web_impact: This page. Calls keep being answered even if it dies.
service_sip_impact: The phone line itself. If this drops, callers hear it ring out.
service_llm_impact: Decides what to say. A restart mid-call leaves the caller in silence.
service_stt_impact: Hears the caller. Without it the agent answers but understands nothing.
service_tts_impact: Speaks. Without it the call connects and nobody says anything.
service_db_impact: Stores calls and transcripts. Calls still work; nothing is recorded.
service_smtp_impact: Notification emails. Port 587 is blocked by your network, so alerts never leave.
storage_recordings_note: Deleted automatically after 90 days. About 4 months of calls at this rate.
storage_transcripts_note: Kept 12 months. Searchable long after the audio is gone.
storage_models_note: Fixed size. Only grows if you switch to a larger model.
storage_free_note: At the current rate you have room for roughly a year.
latency_note: Time from the caller finishing a sentence to the agent starting one. Above two seconds they say “hello?” again — the two spikes are both the same model reload.
bundle_note: Diagnostics bundle the last thousand lines, the configuration file with every password removed, and the container versions. Nothing from a call goes in it — no audio, no transcripts, no phone numbers.
